From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private VPC: clarifying PrivateLink vs Peering and IP allowlist needs

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the deep-dive earlier today. Quick recap and the few items we promised to follow up on so your NetOps/security teams can evaluate the Private VPC option: 

What we gathered on the call:
- You are leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (vs Hosted API) because of regulatory controls and egress routing requirements.
- Primary preference indicated: PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoint) over classic VPC peering, due to firewall/NAT topology.
- NetOps will be responsible for allowlisting Redwood outbound IPs if we terminate TLS at your edge.

Action items / asks for NetOps to unblock next steps:
1) VPC CIDR(s) you plan to use for the connection (e.g., 10.2.0.0/16).
2) Confirm preference: AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint service) or VPC peering; if PrivateLink, please confirm whether cross-account ENI attachments are allowed.
3) If you will allowlist IPs on your egress firewall, do you want us to provide a short-lived IP set for testing or a stable prefix list?
4) Any specific TLS/PKI requirements (SANs, mutual TLS, client certs) or firewall SNI inspection constraints.
5) Point of contact for scheduling a 60-minute connectivity test (we typically do a shared NAT <-> interface endpoint smoke test).

I attached our Private VPC checklist (private-vpc-checklist-v1.pdf) to make the ask concrete. If you prefer, we can also provide a minimal Terraform snippet for the PrivateLink consumer side.

Proposed next step: if NetOps can send the CIDR + preferred connection method, we can prepare the allowlist proposal and proposed test window. We can target a connectivity test the week of Dec 13 if that works for you.

Thanks — look forward to next steps.

—Tessa

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and checklist. A few quick answers from NetOps: 
- We prefer AWS PrivateLink for this integration (security team is strict about peering routes and transitive routing).
- VPC CIDR we will use: 10.2.0.0/16 (primary), 10.3.0.0/16 (secondary).
- We will require a stable set of Redwood outbound prefixes to allowlist for firewall egress. For the initial smoke test, a short-lived /24 set is fine, but for production we need stable prefixes/PLs.
- TLS: standard TLS1.2+ acceptable. We prefer Redwood terminate TLS and provide SAN for private.redwood-inference.com. Mutual TLS not required at this time, but we may revisit.
- Point of contact for scheduling: NetOps on this thread (netops-eng@fintechcorp.com). They will send an availability grid.

I've attached our internal netops inventory and a short list of questions from the network team. Expect a separate email from the NetOps alias with the availability.

On calendar: Dec 13 window looks promising but we'll confirm.

Regards,
Amit
Amit Shah | Head of Platform Engineering
FinTechCorp

Thanks for the context — summary and technical asks below. I kept this high-level for Amit and NetOps; Ben and I can follow up with a formal spreadsheet.

Proposal (test + production):
- Test allowlist (short-lived): 34.192.10.0/24, 34.192.11.0/24 (we'll announce exact /24s 48 hours before test).
- Production allowlist (stable prefixes we use for outbound egress): 34.192.10.0/23, 34.193.0.0/22 (we will provide Prefix List IDs and BGP prefixes as needed).

PrivateLink provisioning notes:
- Typical provisioning from our side: 3-5 business days once we have the consumer account ID and desired subnets.
- We need the FinTechCorp AWS account ID for the interface endpoint consumer and the consumer subnet IDs (AZ placement).
- If FinTechCorp cannot accept cross-account ENIs, we can provide a regional NLB-backed service but that requires additional firewall explainers.

TLS / PKI:
- Redwood can terminate TLS and present a cert with SANs: private.redwood-inference.com and customer-specific SANs if requested.
- If FinTechCorp prefers to terminate TLS on their side, we support mutual TLS; we'd need client cert distribution steps and a CA fingerprint.

Dedicated capacity notes:
- Dedicated capacity is an orthogonal dimension: if they buy Dedicated pools we can still front it through PrivateLink. The difference is capacity is reserved and the cost/commitment is separate from connectivity. A Dedicated deployment may reduce cross-tenant routing complexity but doesn't change the allowlist ask.

Next steps / owners:
- Vanessa: produce formal allowlist spreadsheet + prefix list IDs (deliverable: redwood-allowlist-proposal-v1.xlsx) by Tue Dec 9 EOD PT.
- Ben: confirm whether any additional egress IPs are allocated for canary/test traffic (deliverable: short note) by Tue Dec 9 EOD PT.
- Tessa / Amit: confirm target connectivity-test week (FinTech to confirm availability).

Let us know if NetOps has specific compliance questions and we can route to Security for a short Q&A.

—Vanessa Ortiz
